Ava (PM): Quick sync — we need to settle on the shape of tool-call results for launch. specifically: required envelope fields, what metadata to include, and compatibility rules for old clients.
Devon (Eng Platform): +1. recurring ask from partners: deterministic fields for routing/telemetry and a small stable core so we can evolve extras.
Priya (Eng-ML): Can we capture `model_version` and `schema_version` in the envelope? those are critical for debugging regressions.
Sam (Security): We also need a clear policy for PII in tool outputs. default should be no PII forwarded to telemetry. opt-in with explicit consent.
Luca (Solutions): Customer perspective — they'd like `tool_execution_id`, timestamp, and an attachable `tool_metadata` map for billing/logging (e.g., GPU secs). keep it tiny.
Maya (Design): UX note: when tool returns structured data, product UI should prefer `result.parsed` over `result.text`. need a consistent priority.
Noah (QA): Also define error semantics: transient vs terminal. clients should get machine-readable codes, not just text.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: spec-proposal v0.1 -> staging at 2026-04-03T15:21:00Z
Ava (PM): Draft proposal in-line: top-level envelope keys: `status`, `result`, `meta`, `provenance`. semantics: status in {ok, partial, error}. `result` holds both `text` and optional `parsed` (JSON). `meta` includes `tool_execution_id`, `model_version`, `schema_version`, `latency_ms`. `provenance` = list of actions that produced the result (optional).
Devon (Eng Platform): I like that. couple questions: are we allowing arbitrary nested `meta`? should we constrain keys to strings?
Priya (Eng-ML): Constrain `meta` values to primitives (strings/numbers/bools). no nested objects — simplifies telemetry and indexing.
Sam (Security): +1. and add `content_hash` (sha256) at meta level so we can verify artifact integrity without sending large blobs.
Luca (Solutions): For binary outputs (images, files) we should include `result.blob_ref` and `meta.blob_mime` and `meta.blob_size`. pointer-only model.
Maya (Design): For the UI, include `meta.display_hint` (enum: plain_text, table, json_tree, image) — optional. keeps render decisions consistent.
Noah (QA): Error mapping: `status=error` plus `meta.error_code` (string, e.g., TOOL_TIMEOUT, SCHEMA_VIOLATION, AUTH_DENIED) and `meta.retryable` boolean. Clients can switch to fallback.
Ava (PM): Streaming behaviour: streamed tokens should be emitted as `result.text.delta` until final `result.text` arrives. final envelope marks `status` accordingly. must be backward-compatible for clients that only expect final messages.
Devon (Eng Platform): Back-compat rules: if `parsed` exists, `text` must still be present. clients can ignore `parsed` safely. also add `schema_version` to detect breaking changes.
Priya (Eng-ML): Performance: avoid sending full `provenance` in hot paths. suggest `provenance_summary` (string) vs full `provenance` (array) gated behind verbose telemetry flag.
Sam (Security): Telemetry opt-in: `meta.telemetry_level` in {none, minimal, full}. default `minimal` (only hashes, counts). full requires customer consent.
Luca (Solutions): Edge-case: tool invocation that modifies remote state — we need `side_effect` flag and `meta.idempotency_token`. important for retries.
Maya (Design): Add `meta.user_facing` boolean — if false, hide from end-user UI (internal logs only).
Ava (PM): Launch gating checklist draft: 1) spec doc + examples 2) SDK adapters (python/js) 3) schema_versioning guide 4) QA fuzz tests for schema mismatch 5) telemetry consent flow 6) canary rollout with customer opt-in.
Devon (Eng Platform): Rollout plan: canary to 5% of traffic for 2 weeks, require error rate <0.5% and schema-mismatch <0.1% before ramp. collect metrics: `meta.error_code` distribution, percent of `parsed` consumers.
Priya (Eng-ML): Add regression guard: if model_version changes and `parsed` outputs drop significantly (by >10pp) for a tracked prompt set, auto-fallback to previous model.
Sam (Security): Add cryptographic signature for `blob_ref` pointers (signed URL TTL) and `meta.content_hash` optional signature for high-sensitivity customers.
Noah (QA): Test plan highlights: - fuzz `parsed` vs `text` mismatch - replay with idempotency tokens - binary blob ref verification - streaming finalization race conditions
Luca (Solutions): Docs: provide migration examples: old clients (text-only) and new clients (parse-first). sample stubs for fallback strategies.
Maya (Design): Quick mock: show `parsed` first with a small toggle to reveal raw `text`. will send frames.
Ava (PM): Decisions so far: stable core envelope (status,result.meta,provenance_summary), `text` always present, `parsed` optional, meta primitives-only, telemetry opt-in, idempotency token support, streaming deltas allowed.
Devon (Eng Platform): Open questions: exact `meta` key whitelist? how big can `provenance_summary` be (chars)? retention policy for `blob_ref` signed URLs?
Sam (Security): Proposed limits: provenance_summary <= 1024 chars, signed URLs TTL min 1h, max 7d (configurable per-customer).
Ava (PM): Next actions: Devon to write an RFC with example payloads + wire-compat rules by EOW. Priya to add regression hooks and evaluation triggers. Sam to draft PII/telemetry consent copy. Luca to prepare migration guide. Noah to stub QA tests. Maya to push UI mocks.
Devon (Eng Platform): I can take RFC. will include JSON Schema + streaming example + error code list. target: 1945679600 (internal review).
Priya (Eng-ML): Will prepare eval hooks. also propose a small synthetic benchmark for `parsed` drop detection.
Luca (Solutions): I'll line up two customers for a canary opt-in next sprint.
Ava (PM): Great. if no objections, I'll capture these as launch criteria in the roadmap doc. :thumbsup:
Sam (Security): No objections from security side. keeping an eye on PII.
